svg.text: W7 rev. 4 · Question types 1–6, choice options and rating looks · AWK-20 · 2026-10-14
Each panel: the question on the canvas (as respondents see it, edited inline) and its settings in the inspector. EN; German texts follow the same rules.
Single choice from a long list; searchable. New type “dropdown”.
Search appears from 10 options. Keyboard: type, ↑↓, Enter.
Paste a list: one per line
Single and multiple choice, with “Other, please specify”
Existing types, unchanged; “Other” is an optional extra last option (a switch).
How did you hear about us?
Which product do you use most?
The text field takes focus when “Other” is chosen and is
required then; another radio choice clears it. Drag ⋮⋮ and
edit labels inline on the canvas, as today (M1/M2).
Export: SOURCE as usual + text SOURCE_OTHER.
One tap answers; tap again to change.
A scale with a handle; new type “slider”.
How likely are you to come back?
No handle until the respondent touches the bar:
an untouched slider is “not answered”, never 50.
After touching: the value is shown above the handle.
Keyboard: ← → by step, Page keys by 10 steps.
Short text with a format; the type menu offers them as their own entries.
Enter an email address, e.g. name@example.com.
Checked when leaving the field and on Next. Phones
keep the digits and +; web addresses get https://.
Mobile keyboards: email, tel and url layouts.
Personal data: email and phone are
flagged so the anonymity mode can
The date question gets a mode: date · date and time · time.
time zone) plus the survey's time
Rating: a choice of looks (new “Display” setting); slider stays a bar
Min and max are set per question (e.g. 1–5, 1–7, 1–10, 0–10); the look only changes the presentation, not the stored value or export.
Rating = whole steps you tap (looks: numbers, stars, dots, faces). Slider (panel 4) = fine values on a bar, e.g. 0–100 in steps of 5.
Accessibility for every look: a radio group underneath, each step with its number and label read aloud; contrast and target size ≥ 44 px on phones.

Definition: rating gets display?: "numbers" | "stars" | "dots" | "faces" (optional, default numbers); “Custom…” range with free min/max; publish checks rating-steps-too-many (numbers > 11, stars/dots > 10), faces-need-three-or-five-steps.
Type menu (M1, “+ Add question”) with the new entries · EN
Definition (packages/schema and C#, schema version stays 1: only additions)
type: "yes-no" yes?: {label, code}, no?: {label, code} (defaults Yes/1, No/0)
type: "slider" scale: {min, max, step, minLabel?, maxLabel?, showValue?}
single | multiple | dropdown: other?: {label, code, variable}
New publish checks (same corpus in C# and TypeScript):
Older definitions stay valid: every new field is optional.
Index at publish: “other” becomes an option row (kind other) plus its
text variable; yes/no become two option rows.
Notes · 1 Dropdown and 6 date/time use the shared controls of AWK-19; until those exist, this work item builds them for these two uses only, to AWK-19's rules, and AWK-19 takes them over.
2 “Other” is an option property so a survey can add it to any choice question without changing the question type (and without breaking the variable names).
4 An untouched slider is “not answered”: no default value is ever recorded. 5 Email and phone are flagged as personal data for the anonymity checks (later work item).
Respondent views shown here are what the designer's canvas previews; the runner (later work item) renders the same.
